text: Audit every UI surface in the desktop app twice — once for how it should behave and once for how it actually behaves — and give me a numbered deck of findings.
That's two passes over the same seven groups of screens, then a reconciliation. Here's the plan before anything runs.

plan.title: Audit every YouCoded desktop UI surface twice — once for how it SHOULD behave, once for how it actually behaves — then reconcile the two into a numbered review deck of findings

steps.title: EXPECTATION PASS (fresh eyes, no implementation reading). Work in /home/destin/youcoded-dev.
steps.task:
EXPECTATION PASS (fresh eyes, no implementation reading). Work in /home/destin/youcoded-dev.

Your group: {item}

You are reviewing ONE group of the desktop UI. Do NOT open the implementation
for these files. Read only what a first-time user would have in front of them:
the screen, the copy on it, and the design guide.

Read first:
  - docs/active/design/2026-08-25-ui-design-guide.md
  - docs/MAP.md, the screens section only

For every surface in your group, write down:
  - what a first-time user would EXPECT it to do, in one sentence;
  - what they would expect each control on it to do when pressed;
  - what they would expect while it is empty, loading, or failing;
  - which of those the design guide already answers, and where;
  - which of them nothing answers — those are the gaps worth arguing about.

Rules:
  - One numbered finding per surface, never more than 12 in all.
  - Say what you SAW. Never say what you assume the code does.
  - A finding names the surface, the expectation, and why it matters to
    someone who does not write software.
  - Do not propose fixes. This pass is expectations only; the reconciling
    step decides what to do about them.
  - Do not run the app, open a terminal, or change any file.

Write the report as "## <group>" and then one numbered line per surface,
each reading "<surface> — <expectation> — <why it matters>". Finish with one
paragraph naming the single worst gap in your group.

steps.task:
ACTUAL-BEHAVIOUR PASS (read the implementation, ignore the expectation report until the end).

Your group: {item}

Read the implementation for every file in your group and write down what each
surface ACTUALLY does today: what each control does when pressed, what is drawn
while it is empty, loading or failing, and which states can never be reached.

Then, and only then, open the expectation report for your group from step 2 and
mark each of its expectations met, partly met, or not met — quoting the line of
code that settles it. Say nothing you cannot point at.
